The Police in America Are Becoming Illegitimate, Matt Taibi / Rolling Stone
When is our society going to take a stand and correct the direction we are going in.
In short, when enough people care enough. In this case, it's probably when enough people are directly affected by bad policing.

When it starts affecting upper-middle-class white people.

There is a very large disconnect between the abuse by police and the people who are in an actual position to do something about it. That's why any time the subject of police brutality or abuse of power comes up, people constantly parrot that it's just a series of isolated incidents and accuse everyone of cherry-picking examples to make cops look bad. There's a very strange level of admiration for police officers and this weird Hollywood delusion that every single officer is out there every single day putting his life on the line and single-handedly protecting us from the worst of society, when in reality they have some of the lowest fatalities around and are actually one of the careers with the highest rate of obesity.

To your average American citizens, police brutality is an isolated incident. They've never seen it in real life, and the only time they hear about it is when something so terrible happens that it makes national news. To someone in that position, people like me who think the entire police force needs to be restructured from the ground up starting with the unions sound like we're over-reacting to a singular event. They've never lived in a black community, they've never seen racial profiling with their own eyes, they've never been outside of their own little bubble enough to see the things that people are complaining about. That's not an accident either. Our police officers didn't get to this point by pissing off the wrong people. People who vote, people who understand their rights, people who actually remember that police officers are public servants and not soldiers. Those are the people you want to put your "Officer Friendly" face on for, because those are the people who are signing your checks.

Most police officers aren't monsters who look for every opportunity to flex their authority and live for the thrill of abusing their power. But the more we pretend that none of them are and that they don't represent a drastic need for change, the worse it's going to get.

When it starts affecting upper-middle-class white people.

It already has.
When it becomes harder to comment from your keyboard? The powers that be have no interest in changing until it is in their best interest.

It already is becoming harder to comment from your keyboard. I mean we lost reddit, we lost 4chan. We get shoved off into darker and darker corners of the internet, or shouted off by organized spambots.

The worst part is, they are fully prepared to become illegitimate.

The police and government legitimacy is granted only by us and our beliefs. For them to become illegitimate (which, in politics means authoritative and in control through the use of FORCE), we must only begin to view them as such. Their means are ready for this and they have been preparing for it for a long time.

Edit: It often seems like they are even pushing things in that direction intentionally.

I am probably a little older than Reddit or Voat's average user. I grew up in the 70's and 80's. I have seen our law enforcement evolve into what we have today. It wasn't like this. Now, LE lives are way more important than a citizen's. It was just the beginning for swat teams. They where only used in hostage or life threatening situations. Now they are used over small amounts of pot. The way these cops are trained now, you would think they are on a special operations suicide mission every time they set out to arrest somebody they have been investigating for minor crimes. My grandparents and just about anybody who lived through WW2 would have been in the street's with pitchforks had any of this gone on in the 50's or 60's.

Its not a black white thing. That is what we allowed them to turn it into. We have problems with our Government. The police is the enforcement arm for them. They are stockpiling war toys and it is going to be aimed at us, the citizen. Black, white yellow or brown it doesn't matter.

If the legal system wasn't designed in such a way to perpetuate itself we would have long ago given up on the idea that a cop's testimony carries more weight than a civilian. The justice system likes to pretend that cops are objective arbiters of justice, but they are subject to the same pressures, prejudices, and biases as everyone else.

It is time to level the playing field. If a cop's only evidence of a crime is his word against yours there should be no prosecution.

A note to newish users or those unfamiliar with IRC (I'm not a freenode power user, so any clarification here is good):

In most cases, when you join an IRC server your IP address is made available to anyone on the network. In most cases this isn't a problem provided you have some kind firewall service running locally. But to some this isn't information you want available. If you are one of these people, consider looking into a hostname cloak. Additionally, it may be possible to use a voat cloak to help community members identify each other and show community pride.

To get a hostname cloak on freenode, users must have a registered nick and join #freenode and ask for a cloak. However when you join #freenode your hostname is displayed in the join/part messages. freenode recommends that users use privacy tools such as tor if complete anonymity. Their FAQ is here.
